(By Sri.Shriraja.S, Adv)
 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Claim Petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.

2. Brief facts of the Petition are as under:
That on 09.08.2023 at about 6.30 p.m., on Dandinadibba- Thovinakere Road, near Apanahalli Cross, Dodderi Hobli, Tumkur District, while the petitioner-pedestrian, was walking on the left-side of the road, a TVS XL bearing no.KA-64-U-9908 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell-down and sustained grievous- injuries.

That immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to Government Hospital at Badavanahalli and then to District Government Hospital, Tumkur, where she was treated as an inpatient from 04.06.2023 to 16.06.2023.

That the petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards Medical treatment, Nourishment,
Conveyance expenses and Attendant charges.
3. That prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was an agriculturist, earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, the petitioner has sustained grievous-injuries leading to permanent disability.
4. That Respondent no.1 is the owner and Respondent no.2 is the insurer of the offending-vehicle and both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to Petitioner.
Hence this Petition.
5. In pursuance of notice, Respondent no.1 & 2 appeared through their respective counsel and have filed their objections to the main petition.

6. In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.1-Owner has stated that the TVS XL was insured with Respondent no.2 and the rider had valid driving licence to ride the vehicle; also that the policy was valid as on the date of accident.
Thus, it is prayed to dismiss the petition against him.

7. In the Objection Statement, Respondent no.2-Insurance Company has denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner and also that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of TVS XL.

It is contended that the Rider of TVS XL had no valid driving licence to ride the Rangamma vs Thippanna on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40093306/
2 vehicle and has thus been charge- sheeted for the offences punishable under Section 279, 338 of IPC and Section 3 r/w Section 181 of M.V Act.
Respondent no.2 has thus prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 09-08-2023 at about 6.30 p.m., near Apanahalli cross,
Dandinadibba Thovinakere Road, Dodderi Hobli, Tumkur district, in an accident arising due to rash and negligent riding of rider of TVS XL bearing Reg. No.KA-64-U- 9908?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
9. In support of her case, the petitioner has got herself examined as PW.1 and has got marked Exs.P.1 to 16 & 22; a witness has been examined as PW.2 and Exs.P.17 to 21 have been marked.

On the other hand, Respondent no.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.R.1 to 4.
10.
Perused the materials on record.
Heard both-sides.
Respondent no.2 has also filed the written arguments.

11. My answer to the Issues are as under :
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3 :

Per contra, respondents have denied that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending TVS XL.
13.
In support of her case, the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1, a witness as PW.2; and has got marked 22 documents.

Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-10 are the True copy of FIR with Complaint, Mahazar,
Seizure Panchanama, Notice under Section 133 of Motor Vehicles Act & its Reply, IMV Report,

3 Wound Certificate, Statement of witnesses and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.11 - 50 Medical Bills, Ex.P.12 - 22 Prescriptions, Ex.P.13 is the notarized-copy of Aadhar card of Petitioner, Exs
to 16 - 3 X-rays and Ex.P.22 - 5 Medical Bills.

14. A perusal of FIR & Complaint at Ex.P.1 shows that, Badavanahalli Police have registered the FIR against the rider of the offending TVS XL bearing no.KA-64-U-9908 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC and Section 134 (a & b) r/w Section 187 of M.V Act on the complaint lodged by one Maruthi.
The alleged accident has taken-place on 09.08.2023 whereas the complaint has been lodged on 13.08.2023 i.e., after delay of 4 days.
Exs . P.8
& 9 are the statements of Petitioner and Pillion-rider - Maruthi Kumar about the manner of accident.
The Spot Mahazar at Ex.P.2 gives a description of the accident spot.
That as per the Seizure Mahazar at Ex.P.3, the offending TVS XL has been seized.
That Exs.P.4 & 5 are the Notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act and its Reply.
In his Reply, the owner of the TVS XL, has stated that one Manjunath was the rider of the TVS XL and he had no Driving licence at the time of accident.
The Reply at Ex.P.5 shows the occurrence of accident and the involvement of the said TVS XL.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report which shows that the accident is not due to any mechanical-defect of TVS XL.
Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate which shows that the petitioner has sustained grievous-injuries in the accident.
Exs. P.8

& 
9 are the Statement of witnesses.

15. Ex.P.10 is the Charge sheet which discloses that after thorough investigation, the I.O has filed the charge-sheet against Manjunath & Tippanna - the Rider & Owner of the offending TVS XL for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC and Section 3 r/w Section 181, Section 5 r/w Section 180 of M.V Act.
On the contrary, respondent no.2 had although denied the negligence of the rider of the offending TVS XL, it has not examined the rider to prove its contention.

Further,
Respondent no.1/Owner has not set- up any specific defence regarding 'negligence'
. But after thorough investigation, the I.O. has filed the Charge-sheet against the rider of the offending TVS XL and the said charge sheet has not been challenged by its rider.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending-vehicle, in which the petitioner has sustained grievous-injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the "Affirmative".
16. Issue No.2:-
Having proved that the accident was due to the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending TVS XL, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

17. The petitioner who is examined as PW.1 has deposed that due to the accident, she sustained fracture Type II open BB right leg mid 1/3rd head injury and abrasion over stomach, ribs, legs,
hands, chest, forehead, face hip joint and other parts of the body.
That she has been treated as an inpatient at Government Hospital, Badavanahalli, and then at Govenrment Hospital, Tumkur from 09.08.2023 to 18.08.2023.

This evidence of PW.1 is also supported by the evidence of the doctor who has been examined as PW.2.
18.
That as per the Wound Certificate at Ex.P.7 and the evidence of PW.2 who is an Orthopaedic Surgeon, the petitioner had sustained type II fracture of both bones of right leg.
PW.2 has deposed that he has treated the petitioner and that she has undergone surgery with IMIL Nailing.

PW.2 has Rangamma vs Thippanna on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40093306/
4 produced the Inpatient record with Clinical note, X-ray, Recent X-ray film, Old X-ray films (3 in numbers) and Discharge summary as per Exs.P.17 to 21; he has assessed the disability of right knee and ankle joint of the petitioner at 45% and whole body disability at 15%.

sentences.text:
PW.2 has further deposed that the petitioner needs another surgery for the removal of implants and has estimated the expenses for the same as Rs.50,000/-.
19.
Thus PW.2 has assessed the disability of right knee and ankle joint of the petitioner at 45% and whole body disability at 15%.
But considering that the fractures are united, it would be just & proper to consider the whole-body disability at 12% instead of 15%.
20. As per the petition, the petitioner was aged about 65 years as on the date of accident.
In the Aadhar card at Ex.P.11, the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 01.01.1956.
Hence the age of petitioner is 67 years as on the date of accident on 09.08.2023.
Also, as per the petition, the petitioner was an agriculturist, earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
But the petitioner has not produced any document to prove her avocation and income.

In the absence of any documentary evidence in support of petitioner's income, it is proper to take her notional-income as Rs.16,000/- as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, since the said accident has been occurred in the year 2023.
21.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the petitioner who is aged about 67 years is '5'.
With multiplier of 5, income of Rs.16,000/- per month and the whole-body disability of Petitioner at 12%.
The future loss of income works out at: Rs.16,000 X 12 X 5X 12/100 = Rs.1,15,200/- and the petitioner is entitled for the same as compensation under the Head 'Future loss of income'.

22. The petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in her evidence that she has been treated as an inpatient at Government Hospital, Badavanahalli and Govenrment Hospital, Tumkur; that she has been treated as an inpatient - from 09.08.2023 to 18.08.2023.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 10 days only.

Owing to the nature of injuries sustained,
the petitioner has undergone Pain, Shock & Suffering.
He is thus entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards 'Pain, Shock and Suffering'.
The petitioner having lost the usual comfort of life due to the injuries sustained, is entitled for a sum of Rs.25,000/- under the Head 'Loss of Amenities'.
Further, the petitioner might have laid-up for atleast 2 months due to multiple-fractures.

Thus considering the laid-up period as 2 months, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- (@ Rs.16,000/- per month) under the head 'Loss of income during the Laid-up period'.
23.
Admittedly, during the laid-up period of 2 months, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and might have spent some amount towards extra diet, nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.10,000/-
towards Attendant's charges, extra Diet and Nourishment and Conveyance would be just and reasonable.

In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/- (Rs.10,000/- x 2)
towards the Head.

sentences.text: The Petitioner has deposed that she has spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards Medical-expenses.
She has produced 50 Medical Bills at Ex.P.11 to as sum of Rs.64,180/-, 5 Medical Bills at Ex.P.22 to a sum of Rs.45,530/-, totally to a sum of Rs.1,09,710/-.
Respondent no.2 has disputed the medical bills.

Among the Medical Bills, the only acceptable Medical bill is the I.P.Bill in the Case Sheet at Ex.P.17 to a sum of Rs.19,500/- Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.19,500/- as compensation under the Head Medical Expenses.
25.

Further, as already discussed above, the Doctor who is examined as PW.2 has deposed that the petitioner requires one more surgery for the removal of implants and it costs around Rs.50,000/-
Hence the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the Head 'Future Medical expenses'.
26.

Considering the above aspects, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation as under :
1. Future Loss of Income Rs. 1,15,200/-
2. Pain & Suffering Rs. 40,000/-
3. Loss of Amenities Rs. 25,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid-up Rs. 32,000/-
period 5. Food,Nourishment, Rs. 20,000/-
 Conveyance and Attendant  Charges 6.

Medical Expenses Rs. 19,500/-
7. Future Medical Expenses Rs. 30,000/-
 Total Rs. 2,81,700/-
Thus, the petitioner is awarded the total compensation of Rs.2,82,000/- (rounded-off) with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.
27. Regarding Liability : As already discussed above, the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligence riding by the rider of the TVS XL bearing no.KA-64-U- 9908.
As already discussed above, the Rider of the vehicle had no Driving Licence as on the date of accident.

In this regard, Respondent no.2-Insurer has got its Official examined as RW.1 and has got marked Exs.R.1 & 2 - Authorization Letter & Copy of Policy; the I.O. has been examined as RW.2 and Exs.R.3 & 4 viz., True copy of the Notice under Section 133 of M.V.Act and its Reply respectively.

The evidence of RWs.1 & 2 is also corroborated by the Charge-sheet at Ex.P.10 filed Rangamma vs Thippanna on 24 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40093306/
6 against Manjunath & Tippanna - the Rider & Owner of the offending TVS XL for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC and Section 3 r/w Section 181, Section 5 r/w Section 180 of M.V Act.
It is thus clear that the Rider of the offending TVS XL had no Driving Licence as on the date of accident.

28. Further, in support of the arguments that the principle of 'Pay & Recover' cannot also be ordered where the Rider of the offending vehicle had no Driving Licence, the learned counsel for Respondent no.2 has relied-on the decisions reported in: (i)MFA 8960/2009 dated 27.11.2013; (ii)MFA 7945/2009 dated 15.04.2013;
(iii)MFA 100226/2016 c/w MFA 100730/2016 dated 22.04.2021.
Thus, no liability can be fastened on Respondent no.2-Insurer.
In view of the discussion made supra, Respondent no.1 who is the Owner of the said TVS XL is solely liable to pay the compensation to petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue no.1 in the 'Affirmative' and Issue No.3 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
29. Issue No.3

: In view of my findings on Issue no.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.2,82,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.

Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is held liable to pay the compensation On deposit, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.

 Total Rs. 2,81,700/-
Accordingly, I answer Issue no.1 in the 'Affirmative' and Issue No.3 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

: In view of my findings on Issue no.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled for Compensation of Rs.2,82,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.

Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle is held liable to pay the compensation On deposit, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
